reading: Frequency is up, severity is down. 19 provider-level events in 2026 against 8 in 2024 — roughly 2.4× in two years, the worst year in the record — while the median duration has fallen every year since 2023 and the tail is flat: 2026's longest closed event is 90 seconds off 2025's. More often, shorter. That is dependency concentration with better failover, not a degrading substrate. A worsening substrate widens the tail; this does not. That is why the panel carries no dial.

frequency.rule: Counted once per provider per event. A customer incident downstream of a provider event is not a second event.

severity.headline: 5h 45m
severity.note: The tail is flat. A worsening substrate widens the tail; this does not. That is the panel's core read, and the reason it carries no dial.

composition.note: The year-over-year change is physical. Three of the five 2026 power events share one shape: a utility event, a generator or UPS that did not carry the load, cooling loss behind it. A capital-maintenance signature, not a cyber signature — and why this panel cannot be scored into M, which reads fiscal and administrative strain.

attacks.note: Drone strikes; some AZ data unrecoverable
attacks.where: AWS data centre region, United Arab Emirates
attacks.what: Drone strikes damaged the facility; some data in one availability zone was unrecoverable.
Drone strike damaged the facility; the operator declared the region unavailable.

legibility.floor_banner: This is a floor, not a rate. The series is coded from vendor post-mortems, and a post-mortem cannot see inside a 60-day dwell window. The two March events are visible only because they were kinetic. A quiet intrusion that sat two months and was later called 'equipment failure' would be coded here as power.
legibility.counted: Both are counted because both clear the same bar: physical damage to the facility, confirmed by the operator, and downtime that has not ended. Neither is an estimate, an inferred intrusion or a vendor's unexplained failure — the downtime is real and still running.
legibility.rest_note: The other 58 events are vendor-stated equipment, power, cooling, config or network failures, each with a stated cause and a restoration time. They are real outages too. What separates them is that no operator has attributed them to an attacker.

breadth.banner: 1–17 Nov: 1 provider-level event in 2026, 1 in 2024, 0 in 2025. A cluster of customer-facing reads — banks, airlines, a classified network — is not a cluster of causes until independent upstreams are shown. Symptom count is not cause count.

obs.fresh.text: latest observation 2026-11-12, 5 days. Panel prints STALE past 7 days.

obs.breadth.text: window count in the panel equals the coded ledger count; forces the 'one event, many symptoms' line whenever a single provider event carries more than 5M extract reports.

obs.floor.text: the legibility render contains 'floor' and the dwell-caveat string.

m.contradiction.text: PRINTS, never fails. Fires when M reads above 75 while the substrate is demonstrably restoring in hours — a question for the reader, never an arithmetic term.

substrate.physical.text: this panel covers the digital substrate only. No series exists for grid, water or cooling failure as such. That is where 2026 actually got worse, and the layer where a deliberate action would read as an accident for sixty days.

does_not.why: Unit mismatch: event-duration has no defensible exchange rate into a 0-100 load. Inventing one and reporting it to a decimal is the laundering the register exists to catch.
G is the mean of the eight institutional dials. Adding internet reliability would let a bad infrastructure week score as legitimacy loss, which makes G unfalsifiable in the flattering direction.
Four readings, no composite. A composite needs weights nobody can defend and would hide the one finding that matters: frequency up, severity flat.
It answers 'is the class deteriorating'. Attribution stays with the four-discriminator rule in the observation.
